method: agent-enumerated from domain knowledge cross-checked against events/*.yaml and candidate_triggers/*.yaml; primary regulators issue in Chinese/Russian, so anchors verified via English secondary sources (Reuters, CoinDesk, Bloomberg, SCMP, TASS English, Library of Congress Global Legal Monitor, law-firm client alerts). Original-language primary-document retrieval is a documented follow-up requirement.
exclusion_notes: Belarus Decree No. 8 (2017-12-21, effective 2018-03-28) is permissive — it created the High-Tech Park crypto-friendly regime and legalised smart contracts. Not censorship; flagged deferred=true.

Russia 2020 Digital Financial Assets law has dual character: it defines and creates a permissive regime for DFAs while prohibiting use of cryptocurrency as a means of payment inside Russia. Included as P1 on the payment-prohibition prong; primary load-bearing layer is offramp_cex.

Russia 2024-08 mining legalisation law is mostly permissive but contains the regional-ban authorisation that triggers the 2024-12 ban. Included as P1 because the law itself authorises CBR-led regional shutdowns and a mandatory miner-registry; the 2024-12 regional ban is the direct enforcement event.
Bitzlato 2023-01 takedown excluded — US DOJ + FinCEN action against a RU-linked exchange, not a RU-domestic regulatory event. Belongs in federal_enforcement frame.

Russia Rosfinmonitoring 'Transparent Blockchain' tool and KYC-classification platform operationalised 2022-onward — included as P2 because the load-bearing enforcement triggers (specific exchange license revocations, deplatforming) are not yet pinned to a discrete English secondary source.

Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Kyrgyzstan documented restrictions in scope window are predominantly energy-driven temporary shutdowns or permissive regimes. Turkmenistan's 2025-11 Law on Virtual Assets is post-scope. Included as P2 (Kyrgyzstan 2023-11 mining shutdown) where verifiable.

Weibo 2022-08 12,000-account purge identified during research (CAC-led) but the August 2021 specific event in the task brief could not be verified via English secondary sources; the load-bearing Weibo event is the 2021-03 / 2021-06 deactivation of major exchange accounts. Anchored on 2021-03-11 SCMP / CoinDesk coverage.

candidates.title: China PBOC + 7 ministries joint announcement banning ICOs
candidates.rationale: Joint announcement by 7 central authorities banned all ICO fundraising and ordered refunds to investors; first time CN treated ICO as illegal fund-raising. Triggered immediate BTC -5% drop and the September exchange-shutdown cascade. English secondary via CNBC + Reuters local-press citations + LOC Global Legal Monitor.

candidates.title: China BTCC, OKCoin, Huobi forced shutdown of CNY trading and full domestic crypto exchange wind-down
candidates.rationale: BTCC 2017-09-14 suspension, Huobi + OKCoin 2017-09-29 full halt of domestic services. Forced the three largest CN exchanges to wind down within 6 weeks of the 2017-09-04 ICO ban; produced large-scale capital flight to offshore venues (Binance HK launch within weeks). Direct domestic offramp_cex cascade.

candidates.title: China State Council Financial Stability Committee crackdown on bitcoin mining and trading
candidates.rationale: Vice-Premier Liu He chaired FSDC meeting — first time State Council explicitly ordered mining crackdown. Highest-rank political signal driving the 2021 hashrate exodus from China (estimated 50-70% of global hashrate). Triggered the provincial-ban cascade (Inner Mongolia, Sichuan, Xinjiang, Yunnan).

candidates.title: China Inner Mongolia NDRC draft rules ending all crypto mining in province
candidates.rationale: First province-level enforcement after State Council 2021-05-21. NDRC draft published 2021-05-25 with social-credit-blacklist penalties; Inner Mongolia previously hosted ~8% of global BTC mining. Templated the provincial mining-ban model adopted by Sichuan and Xinjiang.

candidates.title: China Sichuan NDRC + Energy Bureau orders State Grid to cut power to 26 mining farms
candidates.rationale: Sichuan was the largest hydro-based CN mining hub. Power-cut directive 2021-06-18 dropped global hashrate ~37% across major mining pools within days. Closes the China-exodus chapter that began with the 2021-05-21 State Council statement. Clean mining_hashpower load-bearing layer.

candidates.title: China PBOC + 9 agencies notice declaring all cryptocurrency-related activities illegal (the comprehensive ban)
candidates.rationale: 10-agency notice dated 2021-09-15, publicly released 2021-09-24 — declares all crypto-related activities illegal including services by offshore exchanges to PRC residents and employees working in CN for offshore exchanges. Likely overlaps with existing china-pboc-crypto-ban-2021 — verify whether existing event already pins this specific notice or only the State Council statement. NEEDS CHECK against existing YAML.

candidates.title: China Tencent / Ant / JD digital-collectible self-discipline initiative banning NFT secondary trading and crypto settlement
candidates.rationale: 14-article China Cultural Industry Association initiative signed by Tencent, Ant Group, JD.com — bans NFT secondary trading, mandates real-name auth, prohibits crypto settlement. Triggered Tencent Huanhe 2022-07 closure. Distinct from offshore crypto ban because targets PRC L4 platform-stack (Tencent Huanhe, Phoenix, Alibaba JingTan, Whale).

candidates.title: China Weibo deactivation of Binance, Huobi, OKEx official accounts
candidates.rationale: Cleanest L4 social-media censorship event from PRC: Weibo (CAC-supervised) deactivated the three biggest CN-language exchange accounts in March 2021 — 6 months before the 2021-09-24 comprehensive ban. Followed by 2022-08 12,000-influencer purge. Anchors the social-media-censorship sub-frame distinct from regulator-issued notices.

candidates.title: Hong Kong SFC Virtual Asset Trading Platform licensing regime (retail-access framework)
candidates.rationale: Effective 2023-06-01 — established the dual AMLO + SFO licensing regime for VATPs in HK; gave 1-year transitional window which closed 2024-06 and led to mass deemed-withdrawal of unlicensed offshore exchanges from HK. Pairs with hongkong-sfc-jpex-block-2023 (already candidate elsewhere). Foundational HK retail-access frame.

candidates.title: Hong Kong Stablecoins Ordinance enactment + HKMA licensing regime
candidates.rationale: LegCo passed 2025-05-21, ordinance in force 2025-08-01. Imposes HKMA licensing for stablecoin issuers; unlicensed activity carries HK$5M fine + 7yr imprisonment. Distinct censorship vector — restricts issuance-layer and locks the HK market to HKMA-approved fiat-backed coins, effectively foreclosing offshore stablecoin issuance to HK persons.

candidates.title: Russia Federal Law 259-FZ 'On Digital Financial Assets and Digital Currency' — prohibition on crypto-as-payment
candidates.rationale: Signed 2020-07-31 by Putin, effective 2021-01-01. Mixed permissive-DFA-issuance + prohibitive-payment-use. The payment-prohibition prong is the censorship-relevant element: bans crypto as means-of-payment and advertising-as-payment inside RU. Foundation for the 2022-01 CBR consultation paper already in corpus. Dual character flagged in rationale.

candidates.title: Russia Federal Law on cryptocurrency mining — register, CBR regional-ban authority
candidates.rationale: Signed 2024-08-08 effective 2024-11-01. Mostly permissive but creates the mandatory miner-registry (only Russian legal entities/IEs) and authorises CBR to ban placements threatening financial stability. The registry + regional-ban authority is the censorship-relevant element that triggers the 2024-12 regional ban. Anchor for the 2024-12 enforcement.

candidates.title: Russia Council of Ministers 6-year mining ban in 10 regions (Dagestan, Chechnya, Donetsk, Lugansk, Zaporizhzhia, Kherson + 4)
candidates.rationale: Council of Ministers decision banning mining in 10 regions 2025-01-01 through 2031-03-15. Includes North Caucasus republics (energy-shortage rationale) AND occupied Ukrainian oblasts (Donetsk, Lugansk, Zaporizhzhia, Kherson) — the latter creates an unusual cross-jurisdiction censorship event under contested sovereignty. Seasonal restrictions in Irkutsk, Buryatia, Zabaikalsky. Clean mining_hashpower censorship cascade.

candidates.title: Kazakhstan nationwide internet shutdown during political unrest — collateral 13% global BTC hashrate drop
candidates.rationale: Tokayev-ordered nationwide internet shutdown on 2022-01-05 during fuel-price protests collapsed Kazakh hashrate (then ~18% global, second only to US). Pure infrastructure-layer censorship event with measurable on-chain consequences. Unique in corpus as a non-financial-regulator nation-state action with cross-layer crypto effect. Templates the broader 'internet-shutdown-as-crypto-censorship' pattern.

candidates.title: Kazakhstan Law on Digital Assets — mandatory mining registration, AIFC-exchange offload mandates
candidates.rationale: Tokayev signed 2023-02-06, effective 2023-04-01. Establishes mandatory licensing for miners, requires miners to offload mined coins via AIFC-licensed exchanges (50% in 2024 rising to 75% in 2025), and electricity-consumption-based tax. Direct counterpart to post-China-exodus mining reshore frame. Combined censorship + capital-control layer.

candidates.title: Ukraine Law 'On Virtual Assets' (signed during post-invasion donation surge)
candidates.rationale: Zelensky signed 2022-03-16 (Rada passed 2022-02-17, just one week pre-invasion). Predominantly permissive but creates NSSMC + NBU joint VASP registration regime with sanctions screening — censorship-relevant element is the sanctions-screening obligation under wartime conditions. Anchors Ukraine's wartime-crypto regulatory frame distinct from EU sanctions on RU.

candidates.title: Uzbekistan NAPP Order No. 32 + Reg. No. 3380 — VASP licensing under presidential decree
candidates.rationale: April 2022 presidential decree authorised, NAPP Order No. 32 of 2022-07-14 + Reg. No. 3380 of 2022-08-15 implemented full VASP licensing with ~$1.985M licence fee + $10.8K/mo operational fee — effectively foreclosed retail participation while preserving sovereign control. Censorship-relevant via licence-fee-as-barrier-to-entry. Lower-priority because LL secondary sources outweigh top-tier coverage.

deferred_for_followup.title: Belarus Decree No. 8 on Development of Digital Economy
deferred_for_followup.rationale: Permissive regime creating HTP crypto-banking framework. NOT censorship. Documented per task brief request for triage but flagged deferred=true.

deferred_for_followup.title: Russia Rosfinmonitoring 'Transparent Blockchain' KYC tracking platform operationalisation
deferred_for_followup.rationale: Operational since 2022 per Chairman Chikhanchin statements but no discrete enforcement trigger with English secondary anchor; load-bearing effect is diffuse rather than event-shaped. Defer until specific deplatforming or licence-revocation action surfaces.

deferred_for_followup.title: Kyrgyzstan energy-driven shutdown of crypto mining farms
deferred_for_followup.rationale: Energy-Minister-ordered shutdown reported by CABAR.asia and Cryptorank but no top-tier English secondary source (Reuters/Bloomberg/CoinDesk) confirms the exact decision date. Hold as P2-needs-check; not in active candidate list.

deferred_for_followup.title: Tajikistan criminalisation of unauthorised mining
deferred_for_followup.rationale: Reported by Cryptopolitan / btcc.com but no Reuters/Bloomberg English anchor; date imprecise. Defer.
